# TriPeaks supplied terminal fixtures

`tripeaks-TP01.png` is the unchanged PNG supplied by Charlie for the TriPeaks stop after final action 146, top-row column 3. It shows the Congratulations reward panel, LEVEL 3,105 and “Click anywhere to skip” at native 1920 × 1080.

The attachment is 2,098,416 bytes, SHA-256 `1cce002aeecee0d167b9b9e0099bce5361bbc9cadb77629ff18216eb670441d6`. The accompanying session log says its earlier saved PNG was 1,333,621 bytes. This fixture preserves the supplied attachment and does not assert byte identity with that earlier saved file. It was captured manually after the guarded stop, so it does not establish the exact pixels of the fourth post-action observation.

The detector calibrates the fixed Congratulations title, fixed skip prompt and separate panel edges. Level, XP, changing reward artwork, pointer and desktop chrome are excluded. Tests retain the original attachment, erase individual stable probes to establish refusal, and erase the variable central content to demonstrate that it supplies no authority.

Recognition alone does not establish a win. The production worker requires a fresh canonical sole exposed top-row card context, the existing cursor-excluded last-action effect threshold, and two consecutive fresh matching reward captures. Partial or unknown terminal animation permits only bounded input-free observation; no completion, Solver or centre click is authorised by an unsupported scene alone. Fresh nonempty gameplay returns to the existing controller policy. Each attempted reward skip requires fresh positive reward evidence; uncertain delivery stops without replay.

`tripeaks-TP02.png` is the unchanged supplied direct Level Up screenshot following action 420, top-row column 2. It shows LEVEL-UP!, the raised OK button and the dimmed reward panel with uncovered portions of its fixed skip caption. It is 1,741,560 bytes, SHA-256 `6b73803c9accba96b821473e3178aa18c2b02312ce635dc91dbe810b53b9bea7`. The accompanying log reports a saved PNG of 1,102,609 bytes. The manual read-only snapshot was acquired roughly 339 seconds after the guarded stop; it does not establish the pixels of the twenty earlier observations or byte identity with the log's saved file.

The direct Level Up detector requires the fixed LEVEL-UP! glyphs and green backdrop, fixed modal sides, uncovered dim reward-panel borders and left/right skip-caption glyphs. It requires the existing raised OK probe and rejects the legacy-low probe. Changing level, rank, central artwork, pointer and desktop chrome are excluded. A progression modal without that reward underlay, a missing probe, two OK probes or a swapped legacy probe is refused.

`tripeaks-TP03.png` preserves the later supplied Level Up screenshot following action 1407, top-row column 2, in a v2.0.9 session that already completed nine wins and restarts. It is 1,744,870 bytes, SHA-256 `3c9ad40600ff5723d2f73df6e1a343edbc5fd0663c5d38c6f1398ac7e9214fa9`; the log reports saved PNG bytes of 1,105,809. The manual read-only acquisition was 164.933 seconds after the twenty-capture stop. The supplied attachment does not establish what was visible in those earlier captures or byte identity with the log's saved file. Its title-overlapping pointer is tolerated by the existing masks; the masks and OK geometry are unchanged.

Reward and direct Level Up are distinct terminal kinds. The same final-card context and actual material effect are required for both, and two consecutive fresh observations of the same kind must fit the existing four-capture confirmation allowance. A kind change resets positive evidence without renewing the budget. Qualified TriPeaks final-card acquisition now permits thirty total post-action input-free observations, including ordinary observations before entering the terminal wait; it does not add thirty observations to an earlier budget. A first candidate on capture thirty may confirm on thirty-one or exhaust its independent allowance on thirty-three. Unknown scenes never authorise input or completion. The shared post-game twenty-observation bound, Pyramid and ordinary recovery limits remain unchanged.

Confirmed direct Level Up enters the existing OK stage without a centre click. Every current or stale OK input in that direct entry requires the full fresh fingerprint, the existing raised point and a fresh QMP probe; STOP after the probe prevents input. After an acknowledged OK, either New Game can appear directly, or two consecutive fresh supported reward panels can authorise a bounded reward skip while awaiting New Game. Reward appearing before OK acknowledgement and unknown or bare-gold scenes authorise no centre input. Uncertain input acknowledgement permits release recovery and stops without replay.

The twenty-six production-QMP regressions use local Unix sockets and are explicitly ignored by default because this execution environment refuses AF_UNIX socket creation. They are compiled with the suite and must run on the Linux host with `cargo test --locked -- --include-ignored` before live launch. Twenty-one native detector, confirmation and production-proof tests run without sockets. Host regressions cover both direct OK → New Game and OK → reward → skip → New Game paths through synthetic calibrated Play, fresh gameplay, Solver and an actionable HALO. Acquisition boundary cases include candidates at twenty-one and thirty, confirmation at thirty-one, transient/mixed exhaustion at thirty-three, unknown refusal at thirty, STOP during the extension and fresh nonempty gameplay returning to ordinary recovery. They also retain uncertain delivery and non-repetition coverage. Compilation and native results are not claims that the transport or live guest was exercised locally.
